data = json.loads(data_str)

# Create model
m = gp.Model()

# Set parameters
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Extract data
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
periods = data["periods"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
costs = data["costs"]
trans_edges = data["network"]["trans_edges"]

# Create sets for transshipment edges
transshipment_pairs = [(edge[0], edge[1]) for edge in trans_edges]

# Decision variables
Q = {}  # Production quantity: Q[p,t]
I = {}  # Inventory: I[p,l,t,r]
S = {}  # Sales: S[p,l,t,r]
W = {}  # Waste: W[p,l,t]
T = {}  # Transshipment: T[p,l_from,l_to,t]
LS = {}  # Lost sales: LS[p,l,t]

# Create variables
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        Q[p, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Q_{p}_{t}")
        for l in locations:
            W[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"W_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            LS[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"LS_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
                S[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"S_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
            
            # Transshipment variables for all valid pairs
            for l_from, l_to in transshipment_pairs:
                if l_from == l:  # Only create variables for this location as source
                    T[p, l_from, l_to, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"T_{p}_{l_from}_{l_to}_{t}")

# Add constraints
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    
    # Production capacity constraints
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t-1], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")
    
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            # Fresh inflow constraint (Equation 1)
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, SL] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l], name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Aging constraints (Equation 2)
            if t < periods:
                for r in range(1, SL):
                    m.addConstr(I[p, l, t+1, r] == I[p, l, t, r+1] - S[p, l, t, r+1], name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
            
            # Waste constraint (Equation 3)
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - S[p, l, t, 1], name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Sales availability constraints (Equation 4)
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                m.addConstr(S[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r], name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
            
            # Demand satisfaction constraint
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(S[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, SL + 1))
            total_inbound = gp.quicksum(T.get((p, l_from, l, t), 0) for l_from in locations if l_from != l)
            local_demand = demand_curve[p][t-1] * demand_share[l]
            m.addConstr(total_sales + total_inbound + LS[p, l, t] == local_demand, name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Transshipment outbound limit
            total_outbound = gp.quicksum(T.get((p, l, l_to, t), 0) for l_to in locations if l_to != l)
            total_inventory = gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, SL + 1))
            m.addConstr(total_outbound <= total_inventory, name=f"trans_out_{p}_{l}_{t}")
        
        # Initial inventory for period 1 (assume zero initial inventory)
        for r in range(1, SL + 1):
            if t == 1:
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, 1, r] == 0, name=f"init_inv_{p}_{l}_{r}")
    
    # Storage capacity constraints
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)) for p in products)
            m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"storage_{l}_{t}")

# Objective function
obj = gp.QuadExpr()

# Purchasing cost
for p in products:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        obj += costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t]

# Inventory holding cost (on end-of-period inventory, r >= 2)
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            for r in range(2, SL + 1):  # r >= 2
                obj += costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - S[p, l, t, r])

# Waste cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            obj += costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t]

# Lost sales cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            obj += costs["lost_sales"][p] * LS[p, l, t]

# Transshipment cost
for p in products:
    for l_from, l_to in transshipment_pairs:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            if (p, l_from, l_to, t) in T:
                obj += costs["transshipment"] * T[p, l_from, l_to, t]

m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Solve
m.optimize()

# Output
print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

Business narrative:
The retailer operates a fully connected lateral transshipment network among all locations. Inventory can be moved between any pair of locations at a transshipment cost, allowing local surpluses to be reallocated to locations facing shortages. Demand remains local and exogenous at each site, and unsatisfied demand after considering local stock and inbound transshipments is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- This archetype extends the single-echelon inventory model by allowing transshipment flows along directed edges given in the JSON; in this case, all ordered pairs of distinct locations are connected (full network).
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. These limits must be respected at each location.
- For each product and period, inventory at a location changes according to incoming production, incoming transshipments, outgoing transshipments, sales, and waste, and must remain non-negative.
- Transshipment flows from a location in a period cannot exceed that location's available inventory for the product. All such moves incur transshipment costs as specified in the JSON.
- Demand remains local: each location's demand must be met from its own on-hand inventory and inbound transshipments, if available.
- Lead times for transshipment are effectively zero in this archetype, so shipments dispatched in a period are available at the destination within the same period.
- The objective is to minimize total cost including purchasing, holding, waste, lost sales, and transshipment costs.

data = json.loads(data_str)

# Create model
m = gp.Model()
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Sets
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
periods = data["periods"]
T = range(1, periods + 1)

# Parameters
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
costs = data["costs"]

# Decision variables
Q = {}  # Production quantity
I = {}  # Inventory at start of period t with r periods remaining
sales = {}  # Sales from inventory with r periods remaining
W = {}  # Waste quantity
trans = {}  # Transshipment from l1 to l2
lost_sales = {}  # Lost sales quantity

# Create variables
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for t in T:
        Q[p, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Q_{p}_{t}")
        for l in locations:
            W[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"W_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            lost_sales[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"lost_sales_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
            
            # Transshipment variables
            for l2 in locations:
                if l != l2:
                    trans[p, l, l2, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"trans_{p}_{l}_{l2}_{t}")

# Add constraints
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for t in T:
        # Production capacity constraint
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t-1], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")
        
        for l in locations:
            # Fresh inflow constraint
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, SL] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l], name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Sales availability constraints
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r], name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
            
            # Waste definition
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1], name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Demand satisfaction
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, SL + 1))
            inbound_trans = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l2, l, t] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
            demand = demand_curve[p][t-1] * demand_share[l]
            m.addConstr(total_sales + inbound_trans + lost_sales[p, l, t] == demand, name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Transshipment limit
            total_inv = gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, SL + 1))
            outbound_trans = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l, l2, t] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
            m.addConstr(outbound_trans <= total_inv, name=f"trans_limit_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Storage capacity constraint
            if t > 1:  # Only for periods after initial inventory is established
                total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, SL + 1)) for p in products)
                m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"storage_cap_{l}_{t}")
    
    # Aging constraints (for t from 1 to periods-1)
    for t in range(1, periods):
        for l in locations:
            for r in range(1, SL):
                # Inventory balance with transshipment
                inbound = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l2, l, t] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                outbound = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l, l2, t] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t+1, r] == I[p, l, t, r+1] - sales[p, l, t, r+1] + inbound - outbound, 
                           name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# Objective function
obj = gp.QuadExpr()

# Purchasing cost
for p in products:
    for t in T:
        obj += costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t]

# Holding cost (on end-of-period inventory for r >= 2)
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in T:
            for r in range(2, SL + 1):
                obj += costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r])

# Waste cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in T:
            obj += costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t]

# Lost sales cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in T:
            obj += costs["lost_sales"][p] * lost_sales[p, l, t]

# Transshipment cost
for p in products:
    for l1 in locations:
        for l2 in locations:
            if l1 != l2:
                for t in T:
                    obj += costs["transshipment"] * trans[p, l1, l2, t]

m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Solve
m.optimize()

# Output
print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

[BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
Business narrative:
The retailer operates a fully connected lateral transshipment network among all locations. Inventory can be moved between any pair of locations at a transshipment cost, allowing local surpluses to be reallocated to locations facing shortages. Demand remains local and exogenous at each site, and unsatisfied demand after considering local stock and inbound transshipments is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- This archetype extends the single-echelon inventory model by allowing transshipment flows along directed edges given in the JSON; in this case, all ordered pairs of distinct locations are connected (full network).
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. These limits must be respected at each location.
- For each product and period, inventory at a location changes according to incoming production, incoming transshipments, outgoing transshipments, sales, and waste, and must remain non-negative.
- Transshipment flows from a location in a period cannot exceed that location's available inventory for the product. All such moves incur transshipment costs as specified in the JSON.
- Demand remains local: each location's demand must be met from its own on-hand inventory and inbound transshipments, if available.
- Lead times for transshipment are effectively zero in this archetype, so shipments dispatched in a period are available at the destination within the same period.
- The objective is to minimize total cost including purchasing, holding, waste, lost sales, and transshipment costs.

Scenario ID: retail_f7_transshipment_v3

[BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
Business narrative:
The retailer operates a fully connected lateral transshipment network among all locations. Inventory can be moved between any pair of locations at a transshipment cost, allowing local surpluses to be reallocated to locations facing shortages. Demand remains local and exogenous at each site, and unsatisfied demand after considering local stock and inbound transshipments is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- This archetype extends the single-echelon inventory model by allowing transshipment flows along directed edges given in the JSON; in this case, all ordered pairs of distinct locations are connected (full network).
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. These limits must be respected at each location.
- For each product and period, inventory at a location changes according to incoming production, incoming transshipments, outgoing transshipments, sales, and waste, and must remain non-negative.
- Transshipment flows from a location in a period cannot exceed that location's available inventory for the product. All such moves incur transshipment costs as specified in the JSON.
- Demand remains local: each location's demand must be met from its own on-hand inventory and inbound transshipments, if available.
- Lead times for transshipment are effectively zero in this archetype, so shipments dispatched in a period are available at the destination within the same period.
- The objective is to minimize total cost including purchasing, holding, waste, lost sales, and transshipment costs.

m = gp.Model("retail_transshipment")

products = data['products']
locations = data['locations']
periods = list(range(data['periods']))  # 0-indexed for periods 1 to 20
shelf_life = data['shelf_life']
cold_capacity = data['cold_capacity']
cold_usage = data['cold_usage']
production_cap = data['production_cap']
demand = data['demand_curve']
demand_share = data['demand_share']
costs = data['costs']

# Decision variables
Q = {}  # Q[p,t] production quantity for product p in period t
I = {}  # I[p,l,t,r] inventory at start of period t for product p, location l, remaining life r
Trans = {}  # Trans[i,j,p,t,r] transshipment from i to j for product p in period t with remaining life r
sales = {}  # sales[p,l,t,r] sales for product p, location l, period t, remaining life r
lost_sales = {}  # lost_sales[p,l,t] lost sales for product p, location l, period t

# Add variables
for p in products:
    for t in periods:
        Q[p, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"Q_{p}_{t}")
        for l in locations:
            lost_sales[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"lost_sales_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
                for i in locations:
                    if i != l:
                        Trans[i, l, p, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"Trans_{i}_{l}_{p}_{t}_{r}")

# Set initial inventory for t=0
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
            if r == shelf_life[p]:
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, 0, r] == Q[p, 0] * demand_share[l])
            else:
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, 0, r] == 0)

# Constraints for each period t
for t in periods:
    # Production capacity
    for p in products:
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t])
    
    # Transshipment constraints: outflow cannot exceed available inventory
    for p in products:
        for l in locations:
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                outflow = gp.quicksum(Trans[l, j, p, t, r] for j in locations if j != l)
                m.addConstr(outflow <= I[p, l, t, r])
    
    # Available inventory after transshipment: A[p,l,t,r] = I[p,l,t,r] + inbound - outbound
    # But we don't need to define A as a variable; we can use expressions in constraints.
    # For sales constraint: sales <= I + inbound - outbound
    for p in products:
        for l in locations:
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[i, l, p, t, r] for i in locations if i != l)
                outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[l, j, p, t, r] for j in locations if j != l)
                available = I[p, l, t, r] + inbound - outbound
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= available)
    
    # Demand satisfaction
    for p in products:
        for l in locations:
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            demand_val = demand_share[l] * demand[p][t]
            m.addConstr(total_sales + lost_sales[p, l, t] == demand_val)
    
    # Storage capacity at start of period t
    for l in locations:
        total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(
            cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            for p in products
        )
        m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= cold_capacity[l])
    
    # Aging and inventory balance for next period (if not last period)
    if t < periods[-1]:  # for t from 0 to 18, set I for t+1
        for p in products:
            for l in locations:
                for r in range(1, shelf_life[p]):  # r from 1 to SL-1
                    inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[i, l, p, t, r+1] for i in locations if i != l)
                    outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[l, j, p, t, r+1] for j in locations if j != l)
                    m.addConstr(
                        I[p, l, t+1, r] == (I[p, l, t, r+1] + inbound - outbound) - sales[p, l, t, r+1]
                    )
                # For r = shelf_life, new production
                m.addConstr(
                    I[p, l, t+1, shelf_life[p]] == Q[p, t+1] * demand_share[l]
                )

# Objective function
obj = gp.QuadExpr()  # Though linear, use QuadExpr for consistency
# Purchasing cost
for p in products:
    for t in periods:
        obj += costs['purchasing'][p] * Q[p, t]

# Holding cost: on end-of-period inventory for r>=2
# End-of-period inventory for period t: after sales, so for each p,l,t,r>=2, (I[p,l,t,r] + inbound - outbound) - sales[p,l,t,r]
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[i, l, p, t, r] for i in locations if i != l)
                outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[l, j, p, t, r] for j in locations if j != l)
                end_inv = I[p, l, t, r] + inbound - outbound - sales[p, l, t, r]
                obj += costs['inventory'][p] * end_inv

# Waste cost: for r=1, waste = (I + inbound - outbound) - sales
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[i, l, p, t, 1] for i in locations if i != l)
            outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[l, j, p, t, 1] for j in locations if j != l)
            waste = I[p, l, t, 1] + inbound - outbound - sales[p, l, t, 1]
            obj += costs['waste'][p] * waste

# Lost sales cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            obj += costs['lost_sales'][p] * lost_sales[p, l, t]

# Transshipment cost
for i in locations:
    for j in locations:
        if i != j:
            for p in products:
                for t in periods:
                    for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                        obj += costs['transshipment'] * Trans[i, j, p, t, r]

m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Set parameters
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Solve
m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

[BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
Business narrative:
Store and warehouse labor capacity directly limits how much inventory can be handled in each period. Labor is required for activities such as receiving, picking, and replenishment, and total labor usage per period at a location cannot exceed a location-specific cap. Demand is local and exogenous; unmet demand is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- The inventory system is single-echelon with production, storage capacity, and lost sales.
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. These limits must be respected.
- Labor capacity: The JSON provides labor_cap=200 per location per period, and labor_usage per product (SKU_Basic=0.1, SKU_Premium=0.2, SKU_ShortLife=0.1). Total labor consumed at a location in a period must not exceed this capacity: sum over products of (labor_usage[p] * units_handled[p,l,t]) <= labor_cap[l,t].
- A simple representation is to treat labor usage as proportional to the volume of units handled, such as the sum of units received, picked, or moved for that product and period.
- Inventory balance follows the usual pattern: previous stock plus arrivals minus sales and waste, with non-negative inventory and lost sales for unmet demand.
- There is no transshipment in this archetype.
- The objective is to minimize total cost (aggregating purchasing, holding, waste, and lost sales) while respecting labor capacity constraints, which may bind in busy periods.

- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]

data = json.loads(json_str)

m = gp.Model()
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

periods_list = list(range(1, data['periods'] + 1))
products_list = data['products']
locations_list = data['locations']

Q = m.addVars(products_list, periods_list, name="Q", lb=0)

I_indices = []
sales_indices = []
for p in products_list:
    sl = data['shelf_life'][p]
    for l in locations_list:
        for t in periods_list:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                I_indices.append((p, l, t, r))
                sales_indices.append((p, l, t, r))

I = m.addVars(I_indices, name="I", lb=0)
sales = m.addVars(sales_indices, name="sales", lb=0)
W = m.addVars(products_list, locations_list, periods_list, name="W", lb=0)
LS = m.addVars(products_list, locations_list, periods_list, name="LS", lb=0)

for p in products_list:
    for t in periods_list:
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= data['production_cap'][p][t - 1])

for p in products_list:
    sl = data['shelf_life'][p]
    for l in locations_list:
        for t in periods_list:
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * data['demand_share'][l])

for p in products_list:
    sl = data['shelf_life'][p]
    for l in locations_list:
        for t in range(1, data['periods']):
            for r in range(1, sl):
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t + 1, r] == I[p, l, t, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t, r + 1])

for p in products_list:
    for l in locations_list:
        for t in periods_list:
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1])

for idx in I_indices:
    p, l, t, r = idx
    m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r])

for p in products_list:
    for l in locations_list:
        for t in periods_list:
            D = data['demand_curve'][p][t - 1] * data['demand_share'][l]
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, data['shelf_life'][p] + 1))
            m.addConstr(total_sales <= D)
            m.addConstr(LS[p, l, t] == D - total_sales)

for l in locations_list:
    for t in periods_list:
        total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(
            data['cold_usage'][p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, data['shelf_life'][p] + 1))
            for p in products_list
        )
        m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= data['cold_capacity'][l])

for l in locations_list:
    for t in periods_list:
        total_labor = gp.quicksum(
            data['labor_usage'][p] * (
                Q[p, t] * data['demand_share'][l] +
                gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, data['shelf_life'][p] + 1))
            )
            for p in products_list
        )
        m.addConstr(total_labor <= data['labor_cap'][l][t - 1])

for p in products_list:
    sl = data['shelf_life'][p]
    for l in locations_list:
        for r in range(1, sl):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 1, r] == 0)

purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(
    data['costs']['purchasing'][p] * Q[p, t]
    for p in products_list for t in periods_list
)

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    data['costs']['inventory'][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r])
    for p in products_list for l in locations_list for t in periods_list
    for r in range(2, data['shelf_life'][p] + 1)
)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(
    data['costs']['waste'][p] * W[p, l, t]
    for p in products_list for l in locations_list for t in periods_list
)

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(
    data['costs']['lost_sales'][p] * LS[p, l, t]
    for p in products_list for l in locations_list for t in periods_list
)

total_cost = purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost
m.setObjective(total_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

labor_cap = data["labor_cap"]
labor_usage = data["labor_usage"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
costs = data["costs"]

# Decision variables
Q = {}  # Production quantity Q[p,t]
I = {}  # Inventory I[p,l,t,r]
sales = {}  # Sales sales[p,l,t,r]
lost_sales_qty = {}  # Lost sales lost_sales_qty[p,l,t]
W = {}  # Waste W[p,l,t]

# Create variables
for p in products:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        Q[p, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Q_{p}_{t}")
        
        for l in locations:
            lost_sales_qty[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"lost_sales_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            W[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t-1], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")

    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, shelf_life[p]] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l], 
                       name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# 3. Aging and 4. Waste
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods):
            # Aging for r = 1 to shelf_life[p]-1
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p]):
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t+1, r] == I[p, l, t, r+1] - sales[p, l, t, r+1],
                           name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
            
            # Waste from period t
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1],
                       name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}")

        for t in range(1, periods + 1):

                           name=f"sales_limit_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            m.addConstr(total_sales + lost_sales_qty[p, l, t] == demand_curve[p][t-1] * demand_share[l],
                       name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")

for l in locations:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(
            cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            for p in products
        )
        m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"storage_cap_{l}_{t}")

# 8. Labor capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        total_labor = gp.quicksum(
            labor_usage[p] * (I[p, l, t, shelf_life[p]] + 
                             gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)))
            for p in products
        )
        m.addConstr(total_labor <= labor_cap[l][t-1], name=f"labor_cap_{l}_{t}")

# Initial inventory (assume zero)
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 1, r] == 0, name=f"init_inv_{p}_{l}_{r}")

# Objective function
purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t] 
    for p in products for t in range(1, periods + 1)
)

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r])
    for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1) 
    for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)  # r >= 2
)

waste_cost_total = gp.quicksum(
    costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t]
    for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1)
)

lost_sales_cost_total = gp.quicksum(
    costs["lost_sales"][p] * lost_sales_qty[p, l, t]
    for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1)
)

total_cost = purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost_total + lost_sales_cost_total
m.setObjective(total_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Set parameters

m.Params.Threads = 1

cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
labor_cap = data["labor_cap"]
labor_usage = data["labor_usage"]
costs = data["costs"]

# Decision variables
Q = {}  # Q[p,t]
I = {}  # I[p,l,t,r]
sales = {}  # sales[p,l,t,r]
lost_sales_var = {}  # lost_sales[p,l,t]
W = {}  # W[p,l,t]

            lost_sales_var[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"lost_sales_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            W[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"W_{p}_{l}_{t}")

                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, shelf_life[p]] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l], 
                       name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}")

    for l in locations:
        for t in periods[:-1]:  # t from 1 to 19
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p]):  # r from 1 to SL-1
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t+1, r] == I[p, l, t, r+1] - sales[p, l, t, r+1],
                           name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1],
                       name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}")

    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r],
                           name=f"sales_limit_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# 6. Demand satisfaction
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            m.addConstr(total_sales + lost_sales_var[p, l, t] == demand[p][t-1] * demand_share[l],
                       name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# 7. Storage capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in periods:
        total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(
            cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            for p in products
        )
        m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"storage_cap_{l}_{t}")

# 8. Labor capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in periods:
        total_labor = gp.quicksum(
            labor_usage[p] * (Q[p, t] * demand_share[l]) for p in products
        )
        m.addConstr(total_labor <= labor_cap[l][t-1], name=f"labor_cap_{l}_{t}")

# Objective function
obj = gp.QuadExpr()

# Purchasing cost
for p in products:
    for t in periods:
        obj += costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t]

# Lost sales cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            obj += costs["lost_sales"][p] * lost_sales_var[p, l, t]

# Waste cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            obj += costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t]

# Inventory holding cost (on end-of-period inventory for r >= 2)
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                obj += costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r])

m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Solve
m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

        for t in periods_list:
            m.addConstr(W[p,l,t] == I_var[p,l,t,1] - sales_var[p,l,t,1])

# 6. Sales availability
for (p, l, t, r) in indices_I:
    m.addConstr(sales_var[p,l,t,r] <= I_var[p,l,t,r])

# 7. Demand satisfaction

    for l in locations:
        for t in periods_list:
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales_var[p,l,t,r] for r in range(1, SL+1))
            d_plt = data['demand_curve'][p][t-1] * data['demand_share'][l]
            m.addConstr(total_sales + lost_sales[p,l,t] == d_plt)

# 8. Storage capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in periods_list:
        total_inv = gp.quicksum(
            data['cold_usage'][p] * gp.quicksum(
                I_var[p,l,t,r] for r in range(1, data['shelf_life'][p] + 1)
            ) for p in products
        )
        m.addConstr(total_inv <= data['cold_capacity'][l])

# 9. Labor capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in periods_list:
        labor_used = gp.quicksum(
            data['labor_usage'][p] * (
                I_var[p,l,t, data['shelf_life'][p] ] +  # inflow
                gp.quicksum(sales_var[p,l,t,r] for r in range(1, data['shelf_life'][p] + 1))  # total sales
            ) for p in products
        )
        m.addConstr(labor_used <= data['labor_cap'][l][t-1])

purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(
    data['costs']['purchasing'][p] * Q[p,t] for p in products for t in periods_list
)

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    data['costs']['inventory'][p] * (I_var[p,l,t,r] - sales_var[p,l,t,r])
    for p in products for l in locations for t in periods_list
    for r in range(2, data['shelf_life'][p] + 1)  # r >= 2
)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(
    data['costs']['waste'][p] * W[p,l,t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods_list
)

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(
    data['costs']['lost_sales'][p] * lost_sales[p,l,t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods_list
)

total_cost = purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost
m.setObjective(total_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize

# Print results
print(f"status: {m.status}")
if m.status == GRB.OPTIMAL:
    print(f"objective: {m.objVal}")

## Problem
[SCENARIO]
Family: F8 (Omni channel and Store Operations)
Archetype: retail_f8_reverse_logistics
Scenario ID: retail_f8_reverse_logistics_v0

[BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
Business narrative:
A fraction of units sold in each period are returned by customers in the next period and re-enter inventory as reverse flow. Returns are product-specific and location-specific, and can be used to satisfy future demand as long as they have not expired or violated storage limits. Demand is local and exogenous; unmet demand is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- The system is single-echelon with production, storage, and lost sales, extended to include reverse flows from returns.
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

- There is no transshipment in this archetype, and lead times for production are zero.

Business narrative:
A fraction of units sold in each period are returned by customers in the next period and re-enter inventory as reverse flow. Returns are product-specific and location-specific, and can be used to satisfy future demand as long as they have not expired or violated storage limits. Demand is local and exogenous; unmet demand is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- The system is single-echelon with production, storage, and lost sales, extended to include reverse flows from returns.
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1) Returned units re-enter as age-1 inventory.

m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

T = data["periods"]
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]

Q = {}
for p in products:
    for t in range(1, T + 1):
        Q[p, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Q_{p}_{t}")

I = {}
sales = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, T + 1):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

lost_sales = {}
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, T + 1):
            lost_sales[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"lost_sales_{p}_{l}_{t}")

W = {}
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, T + 1):
            W[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"W_{p}_{l}_{t}")

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, T + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * data["demand_share"][l])

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, T + 1):
            for r in range(1, sl):
                if t == 1:
                    m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, r] == 0)
                else:
                    if r == 1:
                        returns = data["return_rate"][p] * gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t - 1, r_prime] for r_prime in range(1, sl + 1))
                        m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, r] == I[p, l, t - 1, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t - 1, r + 1] + returns)
                    else:
                        m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, r] == I[p, l, t - 1, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t - 1, r + 1])

for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, T + 1):
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1])

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, T + 1):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r])

for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, T + 1):
            D = data["demand_curve"][p][t - 1] * data["demand_share"][l]
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            m.addConstr(total_sales + lost_sales[p, l, t] == D)

for p in products:
    for t in range(1, T + 1):
        cap = data["production_cap"][p][t - 1]
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= cap)

for l in locations:
    for t in range(1, T + 1):
        total_inv = gp.quicksum(data["cold_usage"][p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)) for p in products)
        m.addConstr(total_inv <= data["cold_capacity"][l])

obj = gp.quicksum(data["costs"]["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in range(1, T + 1))
obj += gp.quicksum(data["costs"]["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r]) for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, T + 1) for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1))

obj += gp.quicksum(data["costs"]["lost_sales"][p] * lost_sales[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, T + 1))

m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.status}")
if m.status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.objVal}")

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Create model
m = gp.Model()

# Set parameters
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Extract data
products = data['products']
locations = data['locations']
num_periods = data['periods']
periods = range(1, num_periods + 1)
shelf_life = data['shelf_life']
cold_capacity = data['cold_capacity']
cold_usage = data['cold_usage']
production_cap = data['production_cap']
return_rate = data['return_rate']
demand_curve = data['demand_curve']
demand_share = data['demand_share']
costs = data['costs']

# Define variables
Q = m.addVars(products, periods, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="Q")

# Create indices for sales and I: (p, l, t, r) for each p, l, t, and r from 1 to shelf_life[p]
sales_I_indices = []
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                sales_I_indices.append((p, l, t, r))

sales = m.addVars(sales_I_indices, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="sales")
I = m.addVars(sales_I_indices, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="I")

# Lost sales and waste variables
LS_W_indices = [(p, l, t) for p in products for l in locations for t in periods]
LS = m.addVars(LS_W_indices, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="LS", lb=0)
W = m.addVars(LS_W_indices, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name="W", lb=0)

# Constraints for t=1
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        # I for r=SL from production
        m.addConstr(I[p, l, 1, sl] == Q[p, 1] * demand_share[l])
        # I for r=1 to SL-1 is 0
        for r in range(1, sl):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 1, r] == 0)

# Constraints for t from 2 to T
for t in range(2, num_periods + 1):
    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for l in locations:
            # I for r=SL from production
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l])
            # I for r=1: from aging and returns
            sum_sales_prev = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t-1, r] for r in range(1, sl + 1))
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, 1] == (I[p, l, t-1, 2] - sales[p, l, t-1, 2]) + return_rate[p] * sum_sales_prev)
            # I for r=2 to SL-1 from aging
            for r in range(2, sl):
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, r] == I[p, l, t-1, r+1] - sales[p, l, t-1, r+1])

# Sales constraints: sales <= I
for p, l, t, r in sales_I_indices:
    m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r])

# Lost sales constraints
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            D = demand_curve[p][t-1] * demand_share[l]
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            m.addConstr(LS[p, l, t] >= D - total_sales)

# Waste constraints
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1])

# Production capacity constraints
for p in products:
    for t in periods:
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t-1])

# Cold storage constraints
for l in locations:
    for t in periods:
        total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)) for p in products)
        m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= cold_capacity[l])

# Objective function
purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(costs['purchasing'][p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in periods)
holding_cost = gp.quicksum(costs['inventory'][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r]) for p in products for l in locations for t in periods for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1))
waste_cost = gp.quicksum(costs['waste'][p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)
lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(costs['lost_sales'][p] * LS[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

total_cost = purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost
m.setObjective(total_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Solve
m.optimize()

# Print status and objective
print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

            m.addConstr(total_sales + lost_sales[p, l, t] == demand)

for p in products:
    for t in periods:
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t-1])

# 8. Storage capacity: sum_p cold_usage[p] * (sum_r I[p,l,t,r]) <= cold_capacity[l] for each l,t
for l in locations:
    for t in periods:
        total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p]+1)) for p in products)

data = json.loads(data_str)

# Create model
m = gp.Model()
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Extract data
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
periods = data["periods"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
labor_usage = data["labor_usage"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
labor_cap = data["labor_cap"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
costs = data["costs"]

# Create decision variables
Q = {}  # Production quantity
I = {}  # Inventory at start of period
sales = {}  # Sales
lost_sales = {}  # Lost sales
W = {}  # Waste

# Initialize variables
for p in products:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        Q[p, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Q_{p}_{t}")
        
        for l in locations:
            lost_sales[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"lost_sales_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            W[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"W_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# Add constraints
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        # Production capacity constraint
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t-1], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")
        
        for l in locations:
            # Fresh inflow constraint
            if t <= periods:
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l], name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Demand satisfaction constraint
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, sl + 1))
            m.addConstr(total_sales + lost_sales[p, l, t] == demand_curve[p][t-1] * demand_share[l], 
                       name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Sales limit constraints
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r], name=f"sales_limit_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
            
            # Waste constraint
            if t <= periods:
                m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1], name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            # Aging constraints
            if t < periods:
                for r in range(1, sl):
                    m.addConstr(I[p, l, t+1, r] == I[p, l, t, r+1] - sales[p, l, t, r+1], 
                               name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# Storage capacity constraints
for l in locations:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        storage_usage = gp.quicksum(cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)) 
                                  for p in products)
        m.addConstr(storage_usage <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"storage_cap_{l}_{t}")

# Labor capacity constraints
for l in locations:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        labor_usage_total = gp.quicksum(labor_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)) 
                                     for p in products)
        m.addConstr(labor_usage_total <= labor_cap[l][t-1], name=f"labor_cap_{l}_{t}")

# Set objective function
purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in range(1, periods + 1))
inventory_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r]) 
                           for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1) 
                           for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1))
waste_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1))
lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["lost_sales"][p] * lost_sales[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1))

total_cost = purchasing_cost + inventory_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost
m.setObjective(total_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Solve the model
m.optimize()

# Print results
print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

sales = {}  # Sales during period t for inventory with r periods remaining

        m.addConstr(total_labor <= labor_cap[l][t])

# Initial inventory: for t=0, I[p,l,0,r] = 0 for r < shelf_life[p]
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, shelf_life[p]):  # r from 1 to SL-1

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(costs['inventory'][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r]) for p in products for l in locations for t in periods for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1))
waste_cost = gp.quicksum(costs['waste'][p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)
lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(costs['lost_sales'][p] * L[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)
total_cost = purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost
m.setObjective(total_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Solve
m.optimize()

# Print results
print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

Demand from walk-in and online customers is aggregated into a single local demand stream per product and location, and unmet demand is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- The inventory structure is single-echelon with local demand at each location, storage capacity, and lost sales.
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. Storage capacities are scaled to 5x normal values to accommodate dual-channel operations.
- Labor capacity: The JSON provides labor_cap=500 per location per period, with higher labor_usage per product (SKU_Basic=0.5, SKU_Premium=0.8, SKU_ShortLife=0.6) reflecting the additional work from online fulfillment.
- Stores conceptually serve two demand streams, but the model treats them as a single aggregated demand per product and location.
- Inventory remains non-negative and is updated from previous stock and production, minus sales and waste.
- There is no transshipment; lead times are zero, and substitution behavior remains as encoded.
- The objective is to minimize total cost (aggregating purchasing, holding, waste, and lost sales) while balancing higher labor intensity against increased capacity.

        for t in periods:
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * data["demand_share"][l])

    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            if t < data["periods"]:
                for r in range(1, sl):

for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1])

for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r])

for j in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            D_jlt = data["demand_curve"][j][t - 1] * data["demand_share"][l]
            allowed_p = [p for p in products if (p, j) in allowed_pairs]
            m.addConstr(gp.quicksum(A[p, j, l, t] for p in allowed_p) + lost_sales[j, l, t] == D_jlt)

    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            allowed_j = [j for j in products if (p, j) in allowed_pairs]
            total_sales_p = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            m.addConstr(gp.quicksum(A[p, j, l, t] for j in allowed_j) <= total_sales_p)

    for t in periods:
        total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(data["cold_usage"][p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)) for p in products)
        m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= data["cold_capacity"][l])

    for t in periods:
        labor_usage_total = gp.quicksum(data["labor_usage"][p] * gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)) for p in products)
        m.addConstr(labor_usage_total <= data["labor_cap"][l][t - 1])

    for t in periods:
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= data["production_cap"][p][t - 1])

purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(data["costs"]["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in periods)
holding_cost = gp.quicksum(data["costs"]["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r]) for p in products for l in locations for t in periods for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1))

total_cost = purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost
m.setObjective(total_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

)

)

)

shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
costs = data["costs"]
waste_limit_pct = data["constraints"]["waste_limit_pct"]

# Create decision variables
Q = {}  # Production quantity: Q[p,t]
I = {}  # Inventory: I[p,l,t,r]
sales = {}  # Sales: sales[p,l,t,r]
W = {}  # Waste: W[p,l,t]
lost_sales = {}  # Lost sales: lost_sales[p,l,t]
substitution = {}  # Substitution: substitution[p,l,t] (Basic -> Premium)

# Initialize variables
for p in products:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):

                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# Add constraints
# 1. Fresh inflow constraint
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, SL] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l], 
                       name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# 2. Aging constraint
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods):
            for r in range(1, SL):
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t+1, r] == I[p, l, t, r+1] - sales[p, l, t, r+1],
                           name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# 3. Waste definition constraint
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1],
                       name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# 4. Sales availability constraint

    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r],
                           name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# 5. Storage capacity constraint
for l in locations:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(
            cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            for p in products
        )
        m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"storage_cap_{l}_{t}")

# 6. Waste limit constraint
total_waste = gp.quicksum(W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1))
total_demand = gp.quicksum(
    demand_curve[p][t-1] * demand_share[l] 
    for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1)
)
m.addConstr(total_waste <= waste_limit_pct * total_demand, name="waste_limit")

# 7. Production capacity constraint
for p in products:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t-1], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")

# 8. Demand fulfillment constraint
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            
            if p == "SKU_Premium":
                # Premium can be substituted by Basic
                sub_in = substitution[p, l, t]
                demand_constraint = total_sales + sub_in - lost_sales[p, l, t] == demand_curve[p][t-1] * demand_share[l]
                m.addConstr(demand_constraint, name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            elif p == "SKU_Basic":
                # Basic can substitute Premium
                sub_out = gp.quicksum(substitution["SKU_Premium", l, t] for l_prime in locations if l_prime == l)
                demand_constraint = total_sales - sub_out - lost_sales[p, l, t] == demand_curve[p][t-1] * demand_share[l]
                m.addConstr(demand_constraint, name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            else:
                # ShortLife has no substitution
                demand_constraint = total_sales - lost_sales[p, l, t] == demand_curve[p][t-1] * demand_share[l]
                m.addConstr(demand_constraint, name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# Substitution constraint: substitution cannot exceed available Basic inventory
for l in locations:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        if ("SKU_Basic", "SKU_Premium") in [tuple(edge) for edge in data["network"]["sub_edges"]]:
            total_basic_avail = gp.quicksum(
                sales["SKU_Basic", l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life["SKU_Basic"] + 1)
            ) + lost_sales["SKU_Basic", l, t]
            m.addConstr(substitution["SKU_Premium", l, t] <= total_basic_avail, 
                       name=f"sub_limit_{l}_{t}")

# Set objective function
purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in range(1, periods + 1)
)

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r])
    for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1) 
    for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)  # r >= 2 only
)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1)
)

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["lost_sales"][p] * lost_sales[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in range(1, periods + 1)
)

total_cost = purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost
m.setObjective(total_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Solve the model
m.optimize()

# Print results
print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

- Locations L = ["DC1", "DC2", "DC3", "DC4", "DC5"]
- Periods T = 1..20
- Remaining life R[p] = 1..shelf_life[p] for each product p

**Parameters:**
- shelf_life[p], cold_capacity[l], cold_usage[p]
- production_cap[p,t], demand_curve[p,t], demand_share[l]
- cost parameters: purchasing[p], inventory[p], waste[p], lost_sales[p]
- waste_limit_pct = 0.02

**Decision Variables:**
- Q[p,t] ≥ 0 (continuous) - production quantity
- I[p,l,t,r] ≥ 0 (continuous) - inventory at start of period t with r periods remaining
- sales[p,l,t,r] ≥ 0 (continuous) - sales from inventory with r periods remaining
- W[p,l,t] ≥ 0 (continuous) - waste quantity
- lost_sales_qty[p,l,t] ≥ 0 (continuous) - unmet demand

**Variable Type Reasoning:**
All variables are CONTINUOUS because:
- The problem involves quantities of goods that can be fractional
- No indication that items must be integer (pack_size = 1 suggests continuous)
- Production caps and demands are integers but can be treated as continuous bounds

**Constraints:**
1. **Fresh inflow:** I[p,l,t,SL[p]] = Q[p,t] × demand_share[l]
2. **Aging:** I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL[p]-1
3. **Waste definition:** W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
4. **Sales limit:** sales[p,l,t,r] ≤ I[p,l,t,r]
5. **Production capacity:** Q[p,t] ≤ production_cap[p][t-1] (0-indexed adjustment)
6. **Storage capacity:** ∑ₚ (cold_usage[p] × ∑ᵣ I[p,l,t,r]) ≤ cold_capacity[l]
7. **Waste limit:** ∑(W) ≤ 0.02 × ∑(demand)
8. **Demand fulfillment with substitution:** 
   - For SKU_Premium: sales + substitution ≤ demand
   - For SKU_Basic: sales - substitution ≤ demand

**Objective:**
Minimize ∑(purchasing[p] × Q[p,t]) + ∑(inventory[p] × I[p,l,t,r]) + ∑(waste[p] × W[p,l,t]) + ∑(lost_sales[p] × lost_sales_qty[p,l,t])

data = json.loads(data_str)

# Create model
m = gp.Model()

# Set parameters
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Extract data
periods = data["periods"]
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
costs = data["costs"]
waste_limit_pct = data["constraints"]["waste_limit_pct"]

# Create decision variables
Q = {}  # Production quantity Q[p,t]
I = {}  # Inventory I[p,l,t,r]
sales = {}  # Sales sales[p,l,t,r]
W = {}  # Waste W[p,l,t]
lost_sales_qty = {}  # Lost sales lost_sales_qty[p,l,t]
substitution = {}  # Substitution from Basic to Premium

# Initialize variables
for p in products:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        Q[p, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Q_{p}_{t}")
        
        for l in locations:
            lost_sales_qty[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"lost_sales_{p}_{l}_{t}")
            
            if p == "SKU_Basic":
                substitution[l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"sub_{l}_{t}")
            
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")
            
            W[p, l, t] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"W_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# Set objective function

for p in products:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        obj += costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t]
        
        for l in locations:
            obj += costs["lost_sales"][p] * lost_sales_qty[p, l, t]
            obj += costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t]
            
            # Inventory holding cost (only for r >= 2)
            for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                obj += costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r])

m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Constraints

# 1. Production capacity constraints
for p in products:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t-1], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")

# 2. Fresh inflow constraints

    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        for l in locations:
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, shelf_life[p]] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l], 
                       name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# 3. Aging constraints

    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods):
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p]):
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t+1, r] == I[p, l, t, r+1] - sales[p, l, t, r+1],
                           name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# 4. Waste constraints
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1],
                       name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# 5. Sales availability constraints
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r],
                           name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# 6. Storage capacity constraints
for l in locations:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        total_inventory = gp.QuadExpr()
        for p in products:
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
                total_inventory += cold_usage[p] * I[p, l, t, r]
        m.addConstr(total_inventory <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"storage_cap_{l}_{t}")

# 7. Waste limit constraint
total_waste = gp.QuadExpr()
total_demand = 0

for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, periods + 1):
            total_waste += W[p, l, t]

for p in products:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        total_demand += demand_curve[p][t-1]

m.addConstr(total_waste <= waste_limit_pct * total_demand, name="waste_limit")

# 8. Demand fulfillment with substitution
for l in locations:
    for t in range(1, periods + 1):
        # SKU_Premium demand
        premium_demand = demand_curve["SKU_Premium"][t-1] * demand_share[l]
        premium_sales = gp.QuadExpr()
        for r in range(1, shelf_life["SKU_Premium"] + 1):
            premium_sales += sales["SKU_Premium", l, t, r]
        
        m.addConstr(premium_sales + substitution[l, t] + lost_sales_qty["SKU_Premium", l, t] == premium_demand,
                   name=f"premium_demand_{l}_{t}")
        
        # SKU_Basic demand
        basic_demand = demand_curve["SKU_Basic"][t-1] * demand_share[l]
        basic_sales = gp.QuadExpr()
        for r in range(1, shelf_life["SKU_Basic"] + 1):
            basic_sales += sales["SKU_Basic", l, t, r]
        
        m.addConstr(basic_sales - substitution[l, t] + lost_sales_qty["SKU_Basic", l, t] == basic_demand,
                   name=f"basic_demand_{l}_{t}")
        
        # SKU_ShortLife demand
        shortlife_demand = demand_curve["SKU_ShortLife"][t-1] * demand_share[l]
        shortlife_sales = gp.QuadExpr()
        for r in range(1, shelf_life["SKU_ShortLife"] + 1):
            shortlife_sales += sales["SKU_ShortLife", l, t, r]
        
        m.addConstr(shortlife_sales + lost_sales_qty["SKU_ShortLife", l, t] == shortlife_demand,
                   name=f"shortlife_demand_{l}_{t}")

# 9. Initial inventory (assume zero)
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 1, r] == 0, name=f"init_inv_{p}_{l}_{r}")

# Solve the model
m.optimize()

# Print results
print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

locations = data["locations"]
periods = list(range(1, data["periods"] + 1))
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
costs = data["costs"]
constraints = data["constraints"]
network = data["network"]
waste_limit_pct = constraints["waste_limit_pct"]

I_index = []
sales_index = []
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):

                sales_index.append((p, l, t, r))

W_index = [(p, l, t) for p in products for l in locations for t in periods]
lost_sales_index = [(p, l, t) for p in products for l in locations for t in periods]
X_index = [(p, q, l, t) for p in products for q in products for l in locations for t in periods]

Q = m.addVars(products, periods, name="Q")
I = m.addVars(I_index, name="I")
sales = m.addVars(sales_index, name="sales")
W = m.addVars(W_index, name="W")
lost_sales = m.addVars(lost_sales_index, name="lost_sales")
X = m.addVars(X_index, name="X")

for p in products:
    for t in periods:

    for l in locations:

            if t == 1:
                for r in range(1, sl):
                    m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, r] == 0)

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            if t < len(periods):
                for r in range(1, sl):
                    m.addConstr(I[p, l, t + 1, r] == I[p, l, t, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t, r + 1])

for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1])

for (p, l, t, r) in sales_index:
    m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r])

sub_edges = network["sub_edges"]
allowed_pairs = set()
for p in products:
    allowed_pairs.add((p, p))
for edge in sub_edges:

    allowed_pairs.add((p1, p2))
    allowed_pairs.add((p2, p1))

for (p, q, l, t) in X_index:
    if (p, q) not in allowed_pairs:
        m.addConstr(X[p, q, l, t] == 0)

for q in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            d_val = demand_curve[q][t - 1] * demand_share[l]
            m.addConstr(gp.quicksum(X[p, q, l, t] for p in products) + lost_sales[q, l, t] == d_val)

for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            m.addConstr(total_sales == gp.quicksum(X[p, q, l, t] for q in products))

for l in locations:
    for t in periods:
        total_cold_usage = gp.quicksum(cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)) for p in products)
        m.addConstr(total_cold_usage <= cold_capacity[l])

total_waste = gp.quicksum(W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)
total_demand = sum(demand_curve[p][t - 1] for p in products for t in periods)
m.addConstr(total_waste <= waste_limit_pct * total_demand)

purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in periods)
holding_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r]) for p in products for l in locations for t in periods for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1))

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["lost_sales"][p] * lost_sales[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

total_cost = purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost
m.setObjective(total_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

periods = data["periods"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
